question: The average of first 160 even numbers is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The average of the first 'n' even natural numbers is directly given by the formula (n + 1).

Here, the total number of terms, n = 160.

Average = 160 + 1 = 161.

**∴ The correct answer is 161.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sequence of the first 160 even numbers: 2, 4, 6, ..., up to 160 terms.

**Formula Used:**

Average of an Arithmetic Progression (AP) = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 
• 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 2
 161
 320
 
 First Term
 (1st even)
 
 Last Term
 (160th even)
 
 Average = (2 + 320) ÷ 2
 
 ...
 ...

 Average of an AP is its midpoint

**Calculations:**

⇒ First even number (First term) = 2 × 1 = 2

⇒ 160th even number (Last term) = 2 × 160 = 320

⇒ Average = (2 + 320) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 322 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 161

**∴ The correct answer is 161.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of first 'n' Natural Numbers

The average of the first 'n' natural numbers is given by the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of first 'n' Odd Numbers

The average of the first 'n' consecutive odd numbers is simply equal to n.

Average of squares of first 'n' Natural Numbers

The average of the squares of the first 'n' natural numbers is calculated as (n + 1)(2n + 1) ÷ 6.

Average of an Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in an arithmetic progression, the average is always equal to the midpoint of the series, i.e., (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.
